WHAT I ADDED (option (i) from my step-1 scope question, proceeding as announced): `assertActivationWorldSeeded(store)` in tests/security/safe-boundary-observation-scenarios.ts, called from openBoundaryStore immediately after seedReadyProject. It reads the world back through COMMITTED production readers — readCurrentActiveGraph, readCurrentBudgetLedger — and throws with the refusing code AND layer on any wrong world. Checks, in order: graph present; revision == ACTIVATION_WORLD_REVISION_ID; EXACT execution-bearing count (never `> 0` — an empty graph satisfies `> 0` vacuously because there is nothing to count); budget root present; every root meter a MEMBER of NODE_ADMISSION_METERS; and each root meter EQUAL to the seeded node's own admissionAmounts meter, read back from the durable graph rather than from a literal. Membership alone is insufficient and the comment says why: a root funded on attempt.count is a member and still has zero coverage for a node denominated in runner.authorized_ms.

WHY A THROW AND NOT AN EXPECT: this file is a SCENARIO PROVIDER, not a suite — it exports outcome builders that `.security.ts` files assert on, so an assertion has no home here, and DoD 4 confines the commit to the two suites. A throw carrying code+layer is the repo's own fixture idiom and it fails the lane loudly.
